page.overview:
What is Viltrum?

Viltrum was the home planet of the Viltrumites and the capital of the Viltrum Empire. At the peak of the Viltrumite War, the Coalition of Planets united to destroy the world, leaving the remaining Viltrumites homeless and their empire without a capital.

Viltrum was a terrestrial planet similar to Earth in composition, but far larger. Prior to the Scourge Virus, Viltrum was an awe-inspiring, sun-lit paradise of fascist perfection, boasting bright blue skies, crystal-clear air, and a pristine landscape dominated by towering, sterile white marble skyscrapers and grand geometric monuments that reflected the empire's absolute supremacy. Following the deployment of the devastating bioweapon, the planet underwent a apocalyptic transformation. After the virus eradicated 99.9% of the population, leaving around fifty pure-blooded survivors, the complete lack of maintenance and industrial collapse caused the automated climate systems to fail, mutating the atmosphere into a hellscape of blackened skies, raging electrical storms, and toxic green smog. The planet became an empty, automated graveyard, most disturbingly marked by a massive, literal planetary ring composed entirely of the frozen, floating corpses of the billions of Viltrumites who had coughed up blood and perished from the disease, forming a permanent, macabre halo around their dying homeworld.

Viltrumite society was a terrifyingly efficient social Darwinist monarchy built on a foundation of fascist eugenics, absolute totalitarianism, and galactic imperialism; however, its structural core shifted dramatically from the historical Argall Era to the ruthless regime of Grand Regent Thragg. Under the benevolent yet imperialistic rule of Emperor Argall, Viltrum experienced its legendary "Golden Age," a period focused on unifying fragmented factions, advancing planet-wide technology, and establishing a supreme royal bloodline based on hereditary authority and perceived wisdom. Conversely, Thragg’s era abandoned institutional stability for raw, brutal militarism; following Argall's assassination by the betrayer Thaedus, Thragg capitalized on the tragedy to initiate "The Great Purge," a horrific civil war that systematically slaughtered nearly half of the planet's own population to root out perceived physical and ideological weakness. While Argall sought a thriving, structured civilization that subjugated other worlds through dynastic right, Thragg's regime transitioned Viltrum into a fragile, desperate, and fiercely aggressive militant empire, one forced to conceal its severe population decline caused by the subsequent Scourge Virus, shifting the cultural definition of a leader from royal lineage to absolute, uncontested physical strength.

Viltrum was composed of Viltrumite males and females, led by the wise but cold-hearted Argall, who helped establish an era of paradise in their golden age, creating technology and medicine that he would expand to the galaxy. Viltrumites erected statues; one with a book, another placed in his very own fortress. It was said that only he was given and deserved statues because of his supposed perfect leadership.

Also known as: Viltrum homeworld.
